concepts.title: Evidence convergence
concepts.meaning: Three evidence fragments converge on one verified match.
concepts.construction: Three horizontal fragments, three traceable paths, one result node with a check cut into its negative space.
concepts.small: At 16px, two fragments replace three and the result node is enlarged; the check remains a transparent cutout.
concepts.strength: The most direct explanation of evidence-level retrieval and verification. The asymmetric fragments-to-result silhouette stands on its own.
concepts.tradeoff: The 16px version needs its dedicated optical drawing; shrinking the full mark loses the check.

concepts.title: Evidence search
concepts.meaning: Retrieval reveals the verified fragment among document chunks.
concepts.construction: Two document fragments enter a circular search aperture; a visible check occupies the lens and the diagonal handle completes the retrieval silhouette.
concepts.small: The lens, handle, and check are snapped to a dedicated 16px drawing with shorter fragment tabs.
concepts.strength: The clearest search metaphor. Immediately understandable to a new user beside a terminal or documentation page.
concepts.tradeoff: The magnifier is more familiar and less distinctive; the lens and check compete at the smallest size.

concepts.title: Connected V
concepts.meaning: Retrieved chunks connect into a verification path.
concepts.construction: Two separate chunks form the descending arm; a short joining path and continuous ascending arm resolve into a V.
concepts.small: The hairline connection is removed at 16px, retaining the separated chunk and bold V silhouette.
concepts.strength: The strongest letter-like silhouette and the simplest small-size drawing. V suggests validation without forcing an R monogram.
concepts.tradeoff: Its retrieval meaning is more abstract; without context it can read as a general verification mark.
